# Viral YouTube Videos Data

A description of the data set to be used for this project will go here. The data itself (which comes from my personal device) is read in below:

```{r}
#Install packages below if necessary
library(tidyverse)
library(corrplot)

viral_videos=read.csv("viral_videos.csv",header=TRUE)
```

Before saving this as an object that can be used for our app, we'll need to make some modifications to a few variables. Namely, we'll convert the binary and time-based variables to a categorical type, as shown below:

```{r}
viral_videos$upload_day=factor(viral_videos$upload_day,
                               levels=c("Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun"),ordered=TRUE)
viral_videos$upload_hour=factor(viral_videos$upload_hour,levels=c(0:23),
                                labels=c(rep("Overnight",6),rep("Morning",6),rep("Afternoon",6),rep("Evening",6)))
viral_videos$viral=factor(viral_videos$viral,levels=c(0,1),labels=c("No","Yes"))
viral_videos$thumbnail_face=factor(viral_videos$thumbnail_face,levels=c(0,1),labels=c("No","Yes"))

#colnames(viral_videos) <- c(
#  "Video ID", "Category", "Day Uploaded", "Hour Uploaded", "Viral?", "Thumbnail Included?",
#  "Duration (in seconds)", "Title Length", "Number of Tags", "Description Length", "Number of Subscribers",
#  "Views", "Likes", "Comments", "Shares")
```

Now, we can save this modified object as an RDS file for usage in the R script for the app.

```{r}
#Saving data as an rds file for usage in app script via a function in readr
write_rds(viral_videos,"viral_videos.rds")
```

# EDA Sample

A tiny taste of what will be included in the app is demonstrated below. We'll mostly focus on contingency tables, grouped numerical summaries based on a categorical variable, and several plots.

## Contingency Tables

Here are some contingency tables for our categorical variables:

```{r}
viral_videos |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarize(count=n())

viral_videos |>
  group_by(upload_hour,upload_day) |>
  summarize(count=n()) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = upload_day,values_from = count)

viral_videos |>
  group_by(category,viral) |>
  summarize(count=n()) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = viral,values_from = count)

```

## Grouped Numerical Summaries

We can also get some numerical summaries based on levels from categorical variables. Functions from `dplyr` will be used here.

```{r}
viral_videos |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarize(Average_Views = mean(views))

viral_videos |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarize(Range_of_Subscriber_Count = max(subscriber_count)-min(subscriber_count))

viral_videos |>
  group_by(upload_hour) |>
  summarize(Average_Shares = mean(shares))
```

One more thing before we move on to the graphs; let's try making a correlation matrix for some of the numeric variables.

```{r}
viral_numvars=viral_videos[,sapply(viral_videos,is.numeric)]

round(cor(viral_numvars[,5:9]),3)
```

## Plots Galore!

A selected variety of plots are described below, ranging from standard histograms and bar charts to a correlation matrix plot for some of the numeric variables.

```{r}
#Histogram for a numerical variable
ggplot(viral_videos,aes(duration_sec)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth=50) +
  labs(x="Duration (in seconds)",y="Frequency",title="Histogram of Video Length (in Seconds)")
```

```{r}
#Bubble plot of Time of Day Uploaded by Day of Week Uploaded
 ggplot(viral_videos,aes(x=upload_hour,y=upload_day)) +
   geom_count() + 
   labs(x="Time of Day Uploaded",y="Day of Week Uploaded",title="Bubble plot of Videos Uploaded at Time of Day Uploaded by Day of Week Uploaded")
```

```{r}
#Bar chart of Videos by Category
ggplot(viral_videos,aes(category)) +
   geom_bar() + 
   labs(x="Category of Video",title="Barplot of Videos by Category")
```

```{r}
#Scatterplot with coloring based on the day of upload
ggplot(viral_videos,aes(x=log(subscriber_count),y=log(views),color=factor(upload_day))) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x="Log-Transformed Number of Subscribers",y="Log-Transformed Number of Views",color="Day of Upload",
       title="Log-Transformed Scatterplot of Subscribers vs. Views grouped by Day of Upload")
```

```{r}
#Boxplot of log-transformed number of views by upload day
ggplot(viral_videos,aes(x=upload_day,y=log(views))) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(x="Day of Upload",y="Number of Views on a Log Scale",title="Boxplot of Log-Transformed Number of Views by Day of Upload")
```

```{r}
#Correlation plot for selected numerical variables
corrplot::corrplot.mixed(cor(viral_numvars[,5:9]),
               upper="number",
               lower="ellipse",
               order="hclust",
               mar=c(0,0,2,0),
               title="Correlation Plot of Selected Numeric Variables in Viral Video Data")
```
